subject: Hosted API — tiered latency commitments & regional fallback plan
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@finserv.io>; procurement <procurement@finserv.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API — tiered latency commitments & regional fallback plan

Elaine / FinServ team,

Thanks for the productive call this morning. Per our conversation Im attaching a short proposal that turns the single-contract SLO ask into a more flexible, traffic-aware commitment model. High level: we propose three service tiers (Gold / Silver / Bronze) tied to request class and optional regional guarantees, plus a formal regional-failover carveout to address DR and cross-region routing during outages.

Key points (summary):
- Gold: p50 <= 35ms, p95 <= 220ms (for requests routed to Gold-capacity pools). Gold is intended for latency-sensitive, synchronous inference paths (e.g., user-facing chat).
- Silver: p50 <= 70ms, p95 <= 450ms (for moderate-latency workloads).
- Bronze: p50 <= 250ms, p95 <= 900ms (for batch/async inference).

Measurement windows and compliance:
- Operational monitoring: rolling 24-hour windows for incident detection and alerts (we evaluate minute-level buckets and raise incidents if p95 in any 60m bucket exceeds target for >15m).
- Contractual compliance: rolling 30-day measurement window. We compute daily p50/p95 per route, then apply a weighted monthly aggregation (weights = request volume per route). This gives stability for short bursts while reflecting sustained degradations.
- Regional carveout: during orchestrated cross-region failovers or cloud provider region outages we allow an agreed transactional carveout up to 2 hours per region per month, provided Redwood executes the documented fallback playbook and notifies FinServ within 20 minutes of cutover start.

Operational safeguards and observability:
- Synthetic probes (per-region, per-route) with 1-minute granularity will be enabled; well surface probe anomalies as part of the Console dashboard view youll get in the trial.
- KV/prefix caching and batching thresholds will be locked per route to avoid unintended cold-start regressions during rollouts.

Attached: redwood-slo-tiering-overview.pdf (one-pager) and an editable mutual action plan that maps rollout milestones to credit triggers.

Ask: please review and confirm whether you want regional guarantees enabled for APAC as well (that will change pricing and the carveout thresholds). If acceptable, Marissa will prepare the contract addendum and the DocuSign packet.

Thanks,

Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosted API — tiered latency commitments & regional fallback plan

Evelyn,

Appreciate the clear write-up. A few follow-ups from our side:
1) APAC: were likely to expand into APAC in Q4. We need the ability to opt into regional guarantees there, but we also need a tighter carveout definition for failovers (Q4 is our busiest quarter). Can you confirm whether the 2-hour/month regional carveout is per-region or global?
2) Credits: procurement wants a clear credits table for breaches that occur outside a documented carveout (sliding scale by severity and duration).
3) Burst traffic: curious how Redwood will treat transient traffic spikes generated by customer batch jobs misconfiguration — do you apply the contractual SLO against raw traffic or after a burst-trimming filter?

Also looping in our infra lead (ops@finserv.io) who will review the probe and routing requirements.

Thanks,
Elaine
Director of Platform, FinServ Analytics

Subject: Re: Hosted API — tiered latency commitments & regional fallback plan

Elaine / team,

Good questions  thank you. Answers inline:  
1) Carveout scope: the 2-hour allowance is per-region. We explicitly chose per-region because cross-region failovers can have very different timelines depending on provider. If FinServ prefers a pooled global allotment instead we can draft an alternate contract clause.

2) Credits: we propose a three-band credit table (Operational, Degraded, Severe) tied to duration and % of traffic affected. Example (draft):
- Operational: single p95 violation lasting <1h -> 5% service credit for that day
- Degraded: sustained p95 > target for >1h and <6h -> 10% service credit for that day
- Severe: >6h -> 25% service credit + executive review and incident RCA commitment.
Well populate the final numbers in the contract addendum; Marissa can run these against your procurement thresholds.

3) Burst trimming: we apply a documented burst-trim filter for contractual SLO calculation. Briefly: any spike that exceeds the historical baseline (30-day median rate) by >5x and lasts <15 minutes is flagged as a transient spike and excluded from contractual p95 calculations, provided the customer does not have an explicit traffic policy that creates repeated scheduled bursts. We still surface these spikes in the Console and treat them as operational incidents for root-cause analysis, but they wont generate a credit unless they persist beyond the transient threshold.

Operational conditions for the regional carveout:
- Redwood must notify FinServ via the shared channel within 20 minutes of cutover start and post a timeline to the incident page.
- Failover must follow the agreed playbook (we sent a link in the attachments).

If that language is good, Marissa will draft the exact contract wording and credit table. Karthik / Ben: can you confirm the quantifiable probe definitions well surface (region/routing tags, 1m probe cadence) so I can include them in the addendum?

Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
